The test image shows soybean stems with prominent reddish-brown to chocolate-brown discoloration extending upward. Key features:
- Stem tissue (not leaf lesions)
- Reddish-brown discoloration on stems
- Dead/dry tissue on stems
- One stem appears greener/healthier compared to the affected ones

Top candidates: **Phytophthora** (chocolate-brown stem extending upward), **Diaporthe** (stem blight), **Rhizoctonia** (reddish-brown lesions at soil line), **Fusarium**.

Let me view reference images for comparison.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Stem disease (not leaf lesions)
- Clear reddish-brown to chocolate-brown discoloration extending upward along stems
- Multiple stems affected
- No visible black fruiting bodies (pycnidia/acervuli)
- No white mold growth
- Dead/dry tissue; some stems have green tissue at top but brown below
- Appears to be lower-to-mid stem region

**Comparison reasoning:**
- **Phytophthora**: Best match — "dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below soil line upward" — the reference image shows similar brown stem coloration and plant death pattern
- **Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown sunken lesions specifically at soil line — the discoloration here extends further up
- **Diaporthe**: Would show linear rows of black pycnidia on stem — not visible here
- **Fusarium**: More associated with root/vascular browning internally
- **Anthracnose**: Would show distinct black acervuli (pin-cushion like) — not visible here
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Primarily interveinal chlorosis on leaves — not the pattern here

The reddish-brown to chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward from the base, with plant death and no visible fungal fruiting bodies, is most characteristic of **Phytophthora** stem rot.
